belief: “I can’t be myself around people unless I use first.”
belief_plain: I can’t be myself around people unless I use first
origins: Some people use because being with others feels impossible without a buffer. The room is too bright, the words will not come, or the real self feels like too much or not enough. “I can’t be myself unless I use first.” That can be social fear, old shame, or a habit that now feels like personality. You are not faking a self when you are sober. You are meeting people without a screen. It can be awkward and still be you. God already knows you without it. Safe people can learn to know you too, in small doses, with help. If you want help, call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. Do not try to stop or withdraw on your own if that could make you sick. A doctor can help you do it safely, and a counselor can walk with you. Needing that help is not a failure.
self: Nobody wants the sober version of me.
I am boring, or too much, unless I use.
I cannot talk to people without it.
If I do not use first, they will see the real me and leave.
God is disappointed by the self I am in a quiet room.
replacement: I can be myself without using first. God already knows me, and I can practice being with safe people a little at a time.
